entryPoint: Topic::isActive() in include/class.topic.php (instance method, no args, called as $topic->isActive() on a loaded Topic ORM object)
coreLogic: Topic::isActive() returns !!($this->flags & self::FLAG_ACTIVE) where FLAG_ACTIVE = 0x0002, a pure bitwise AND against the already-loaded 'flags' property (mapped to the ost_help_topic.flags DB column via VerySimpleModel). Topic::isEnabled() (lines 190-192) is a one-line wrapper that delegates directly to isActive() and returns its result unchanged; no other method in the delegation chain exists below isActive() itself.
consumers: include/staff/filter.inc.php:253 - if($topic && !$topic->isActive()) sets a form warning ('%s must be active') when validating a ticket-filter rule's assigned help topic in the admin UI
scp/filters.php:150 - if($topic && !$topic->isActive()) sets an identical warning on the filters admin page before save
include/class.ticket.php:3686 - Ticket::create()/update() validation: if($topic && !$topic->isActive()) adds errors['topicId'] rejecting the submitted topic as invalid

include/class.ticket.php:4214 - if (...&& $topic->isActive()) gates whether topic-specific dynamic form fields are validated at all for the ticket; when false, topic form validation is skipped entirely
include/class.filter.php:646 - if (!$topic || !$topic->isActive()) adds errors['err'] rejecting an inactive topic when saving a Filter's topic action configuration

include/class.filter_action.php:536 (FA_AssignTopic::apply) - if ($topic && $topic->isActive()) only sets $ticket['topicId'] from the filter action when the configured topic is active; otherwise the assignment is silently skipped

include/class.filter_action.php:561 (FA_AssignTopic::getConfigurationOptions) - if ($topic && !$topic->isActive()) adds the currently-configured topic to the admin dropdown choices list only when it is NOT active (so a stale inactive selection still shows up)
include/class.config.php:1427 - if (...&& !$T->isActive()) adds errors['default_help_topic'] when validating that the system's default help topic is active

include/class.email.php:318-322 - a $topic->isActive() check exists but is inside a /* ... */ commented-out dead-code block (marked 'TODO: ???'); NOT a live consumer, excluded from behavior-preservation scope
include/class.topic.php:190-192 (Topic::isEnabled()) - internal delegator only; no external caller of Topic::isEnabled() was found anywhere in the codebase
inputShape: No parameters. Called on an already-instantiated/loaded Topic model object whose 'flags' integer property (ORM-mapped from ost_help_topic.flags) reflects the topic's current bit flags: FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS=0x0001, FLAG_ACTIVE=0x0002, FLAG_ARCHIVED=0x0004 (flags may have other unrelated bits set concurrently).
outputShape: Returns a native PHP boolean: true if the FLAG_ACTIVE bit (0x0002) is set in $this->flags, false otherwise. Callers use both the direct boolean and its negation (!$topic->isActive()) in conditionals; no mutation of the Topic object occurs.
sideEffects: None. isActive() performs no database reads/writes of its own - it only inspects the 'flags' property already populated on the in-memory Topic object by the ORM's prior fetch/lookup (e.g. Topic::lookup()).
No global state ($cfg, $ost, session, etc.) is read or written.
No lazy-loading is triggered by isActive() itself (unlike some other Topic accessors such as getDept() or getForms()).
No caching, file I/O, or logging occurs.
No object mutation: $this->flags is only read, never modified, by isActive() or isEnabled().
constraints: Must return true if and only if ($flags & FLAG_ACTIVE) is nonzero; the FLAG_ARCHIVED (0x0004) bit and FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS (0x0001) bit, or any other bits present in flags, must NOT affect the result — only the FLAG_ACTIVE bit matters, even when multiple flags are set simultaneously (e.g. active+archived both set, or active+custom-numbers both set).
Return type must remain a genuine PHP boolean (current code uses double-negation !!) so strict boolean contexts and negations (!$topic->isActive()) in callers keep working identically.

Topic::isEnabled() must continue to delegate to the (facade-preserved) isActive() behavior and return an identical boolean for the same flags state - but the new extracted service itself must NOT be called from, or call back into, Topic::isActive() or Topic::isEnabled() (per extraction requirement); the facade method keeps its call site, delegating outward to the new service instead of containing the bitwise logic inline.

The extracted service must not perform any DB query or reload of the Topic - it must operate solely on the flags value already available on the object/value passed to it, preserving the current zero-side-effect behavior.
Method signature must remain unchanged: Topic::isActive() takes no arguments and is called the same way, $topic->isActive(), by all 8 live consumer call sites.

The FLAG_ACTIVE constant value (0x0002) must be preserved exactly as the bit tested; do not confuse it with FLAG_ARCHIVED (0x0004) which is a separate, independently-tracked state used by getStatus()/allowsReopen() but is out of scope for this seam.
harnessInputShape: JSON object with a single field: 'flags' (integer) - the raw help-topic flags bitmask to test, matching ost_help_topic.flags semantics (FLAG_CUSTOM_NUMBERS=1, FLAG_ACTIVE=2, FLAG_ARCHIVED=4, combinable via bitwise OR). The harness constructs/populates a Topic instance with this flags value (without hitting the DB) and outputs the boolean result of calling isActive() on it, so it can exercise: active only (flags=2), inactive/disabled (flags=0), archived-only (flags=4, FLAG_ACTIVE not set), and active-plus-other-flags (e.g. flags=3 for active+custom-numbers, or flags=6 for active+archived both set) to prove only the FLAG_ACTIVE bit drives the result.
